issue.standard_remedy: Map the sub-tier and qualify an alternate
issue.summary: Depends on a single-source sub-tier supplier (North America)

plan.diagnosis: Regal Allied Metals presents single-source sub-tier dependency risk with USD 1,328,950 in annual spend and a moderate resiliency score of 55 out of 100. While the supplier operates in low-risk North America with zero disruption events in the trailing 12 months, the concentration of 27 sub-tier suppliers without qualified alternates creates supply chain fragility and price leverage exposure.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct sub-tier mapping exercise with Regal Allied Metals to identify the 3-5 highest-risk single-source sub-tier suppliers by spend and criticality; request sub-tier supplier names, commodities, lead times, and switching constraints
Issue RFI to 4-6 alternative metal suppliers with equivalent technical capabilities to qualify backup sources for critical sub-tier materials identified in step 1

Negotiate contractual sub-tier transparency clause and dual-source commitment with Regal Allied Metals for top 5 critical sub-tier inputs, securing price protection and 90-day inventory buffer requirement
Qualify and onboard at least one alternate prime supplier across SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, and NetSuite to split 20-30% of Regal Allied Metals volume (USD 265,790-398,685)
Implement quarterly sub-tier risk reviews in Coupa with Regal Allied Metals, tracking resiliency score improvements and sub-tier diversification progress

plan.expected_impact: Mitigating single-source sub-tier risk is expected to protect USD 1,328,950 in annual spend from disruption and achieve 5-8% cost avoidance (USD 66,448-106,316) through competitive pressure and dual-sourcing leverage.
kpis: Number of qualified alternate sub-tier suppliers (target: 3-5 for critical materials)
Resiliency score improvement for Regal Allied Metals (target: 55 to 70+ within 6 months)
Percentage of spend with backup source qualified (target: 25-30% or USD 332,238-398,685)
Sub-tier supply disruption incidents (target: maintain 0 events)
Cost avoidance from dual-source negotiation leverage (target: USD 66,448-106,316 annually)
risks: Regal Allied Metals may resist sub-tier transparency due to competitive concerns or IP protection, delaying mapping exercise
Alternative supplier qualification may exceed 120-day timeline if technical certifications or quality testing reveal gaps
Splitting volume may trigger price increases from Regal Allied Metals if minimum order quantities or tiered pricing thresholds are not met (risk to USD 1,328,950 base cost)
Onboarding delays across four ERP systems (SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite) may postpone dual-sourcing implementation
Sub-tier suppliers may refuse to work with alternative prime suppliers, limiting diversification options
erp_actions: SAP: Maintain Regal Allied Metals as approved vendor but add info record note (EINE) flagging single-source sub-tier risk; create source list entries for new alternate suppliers once qualified
Oracle EBS: Update supplier profile for Regal Allied Metals with risk flag and attach sub-tier mapping documentation; configure approved supplier list (ASL) for alternate vendors
Dynamics 365: Add supply chain risk attribute 'Single-Source Sub-Tier' to Regal Allied Metals vendor master; enable split-purchase requisition rules to route 20-30% to alternate once onboarded
NetSuite: Create custom field 'Sub-Tier Risk Level: Medium' on Regal Allied Metals vendor record; set up vendor bill approval workflow requiring dual quotes for orders above USD 50,000

Coupa: Tag Regal Allied Metals with 'Sub-Tier Risk - Remediation in Progress' and configure quarterly risk review workflow; establish preferred supplier list including qualified alternates with allocation targets
